To multiply two numbers in a given base, first multiply the least significant digits of both numbers. To multiply numbers in a non-decimal base, first multiply the digits as if they were in base 10, then convert the result back to the original base. To divide a number in a non-decimal base by another number, perform the division similarly to base 10, but adjust for the base-specific digit values. To find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two numbers using the Euclidean algorithm, repeatedly apply the process of replacing the larger number with the remainder when the larger number is divided by the smaller number, until the remainder is zero. The last non-zero remainder is the GCD of the two numbers.

To simplify the calculation of the greatest common divisor (GCD) using the Euclidean algorithm, identify if one number is divisible by a factor of another number. Continue applying the Euclidean algorithm by repeatedly replacing the larger number with the remainder of the division until the remainder is zero. The last non-zero remainder is the GCD.
Verify that the result obtained from the previous steps divides the remaining number(s) in the set. If it does, confirm it as the greatest common divisor for the entire set.
